faqs.title: What is HelpView?
faqs.details:
HelpView is a **SwiftUI framework** that adds AI-powered FAQ documentation to your iOS and macOS apps.

**Key Features:**
- Natural language search using Apple Intelligence
- Automatic fallback to text-based search
- Support for JSON and plist FAQ formats
- Beautiful, native SwiftUI interface
- Full markdown support in answers
- Topic-based organization

All AI processing happens **on-device** with Apple's Foundation Models—no network required!

faqs.title: What are the system requirements?
faqs.details:
**Platform Requirements:**
- iOS 26.0 or later
- macOS 26.0 or later
- Swift 6.2+

**For AI Features:**
- A17 Pro or M1+ chip
- Apple Intelligence enabled in Settings
- Language model downloaded

The SDK works on all supported platforms, but **Apple Intelligence features** are only available on devices with the required hardware.

faqs.title: How do I add HelpView to my project?
faqs.details:
**Using Swift Package Manager:**

1. In Xcode, go to **File → Add Package Dependencies**
2. Enter the repository URL
3. Choose your version requirements
4. Add the package to your target

**Import in your code:**
```swift
import HelpView
```

Then use either `HelpViewButton` for quick integration or `HelpContentView` for custom navigation flows.

faqs.title: What's the difference between HelpViewButton and HelpContentView?
faqs.details:
HelpView provides **two public APIs** for different use cases:

**HelpViewButton** - Quick Integration
- Displays a question mark button
- Presents FAQs in a modal sheet
- Includes built-in "Done" button
- Perfect for toolbar placement

```swift
.toolbar {
    HelpViewButton(named: "app_help")
}
```

**HelpContentView** - Custom Navigation
- Embeddable content view
- No modal presentation or Done button
- Full control over navigation
- Works with NavigationLink, TabView, etc.

```swift
NavigationLink("Help") {
    HelpContentView(named: "app_help")
}
```

faqs.title: How do I create FAQ content?
faqs.details:
Create a **JSON** or **plist** file in your app bundle:

**JSON Format:**
```json
{
  "topics": ["Getting Started", "Features"],
  "faqs": [
    {
      "title": "How do I use this?",
      "details": "Here's how to use...",
      "topic": "Getting Started"
    }
  ]
}
```

**Required Steps:**
1. Create your FAQ file
2. Add it to your Xcode project
3. Ensure it's in **Copy Bundle Resources** build phase
4. Reference it by name (without extension):

```swift
HelpViewButton(named: "app_help")
```

faqs.title: Can I use plist files instead of JSON?
faqs.details:
Yes! HelpView supports both **JSON** and **plist** formats.

**Plist Structure:**
```xml
<dict>
  <key>topics</key>
  <array>
    <string>Getting Started</string>
  </array>
  <key>faqs</key>
  <array>
    <dict>
      <key>title</key>
      <string>Your question</string>
      <key>details</key>
      <string>Your answer</string>
      <key>topic</key>
      <string>Getting Started</string>
    </dict>
  </array>
</dict>
```

**Format Detection:**
The loader tries `.json` first, then `.plist` automatically. Just use the filename without extension.

faqs.title: How does Apple Intelligence integration work?
faqs.details:
HelpView automatically uses **Apple Intelligence** when available:

**Availability Check:**
- Detects if Apple Intelligence is enabled
- Checks if language model is downloaded
- Verifies device has required hardware

**AI-Powered Search:**
- Natural language understanding
- Context-aware responses
- Structured answers using `@Generable` macro
- All processing happens **on-device**

**Automatic Fallback:**
If Apple Intelligence isn't available, HelpView seamlessly falls back to text-based search—no additional code needed!

faqs.title: Does HelpView work without Apple Intelligence?
faqs.details:
**Yes!** HelpView works on all supported devices.

**Without Apple Intelligence:**
- Uses text-based search
- Matches keywords in FAQ titles and content
- Full markdown rendering
- Topic-based browsing

**With Apple Intelligence:**
- Natural language queries
- Context-aware responses
- Better search relevance

The SDK **automatically detects** what's available and adapts accordingly. No special handling required in your code!

faqs.title: Can I use markdown in FAQ answers?
faqs.details:
Yes! All FAQ answers support **full markdown formatting**:

**Supported Elements:**
- **Bold** and *italic* text
- Headers (# ## ###)
- Bullet lists
- Numbered lists
- Code blocks
- Links
- Block quotes

**Example:**
```json
{
  "title": "How do I format text?",
  "details": "Use **bold** for emphasis and `code` for technical terms."
}
```

Markdown is rendered using SwiftUI's built-in markdown support for native, beautiful typography.

faqs.title: How are FAQs organized?
faqs.details:
FAQs are organized by **topics** for easy browsing:

**Topic Assignment:**
- Each FAQ can have a `topic` field
- FAQs without a topic go to "General"
- Topics appear in the order specified in `topics` array

**Example:**
```json
{
  "topics": ["Setup", "Usage", "Troubleshooting"],
  "faqs": [
    {
      "title": "How to install?",
      "topic": "Setup"
    }
  ]
}
```

Users can browse by topic or use search to find specific answers quickly.

faqs.title: Is my user's data private?
faqs.details:
**Absolutely!** HelpView is built with privacy in mind:

✓ **100% on-device processing** - No network requests
✓ **No data collection** - We don't track anything
✓ **No analytics** - Your users' queries stay private
✓ **Apple Intelligence** uses on-device models only
✓ **Open source** - You can review all the code

FAQ content is bundled with your app, and all AI processing happens locally using Apple's Foundation Models framework.

faqs.title: Can I customize the appearance?
faqs.details:
HelpView uses **native SwiftUI styling** that automatically adapts to your app:

**Automatic Adaptation:**
- Respects system color scheme (light/dark mode)
- Uses system fonts and sizing
- Follows platform conventions (iOS vs macOS)
- Supports Dynamic Type for accessibility

**Current Customization:**
The SDK currently provides a polished, native experience out of the box. Theme customization options are planned for future releases.

The focus is on **consistency** with system UI patterns.
